display-and-overflow.label: Display and Overflow
display-and-overflow.summary: Control how existing portfolio boxes participate in normal flow and handle content that is wider than its container.

sketch1.title: Protect a wide table with horizontal overflow

sketch2.title: Make form labels occupy their own line

try_display_and_overflow_sketch0.title: Try it yourself: Give navigation links box-like behavior
try_display_and_overflow_sketch0.prompt:
**Problem**

Navigation links behave like ordinary inline text, so their box behavior is limited even though later styling needs each link to accept box-model spacing and sizing.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `display: inline-block;` to a `nav a` rule.

try_display_and_overflow_sketch1.title: Try it yourself: Keep wide tables inside their own scroll area
try_display_and_overflow_sketch1.prompt:
**Problem**

The Projects table can be wider than a narrow viewport, and letting the whole page overflow horizontally would make the site difficult to use.

**Task**

Keep all previous CSS and add `table { display: block; overflow-x: auto; }`.

try_display_and_overflow_sketch2.title: Try it yourself: Put each form label on its own line
try_display_and_overflow_sketch2.prompt:
**Problem**

Form labels currently follow inline flow, which can leave a label and its control competing for the same line instead of giving each field a clear reading order.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `form label { display: block; }`.

display-and-overflow-single-1.title: Check the first box-model decision
display-and-overflow-single-1.prompt: Which display behavior normally starts on a new line and expands as a block?
display-and-overflow-single-1.hint: Choose the property or layer whose location matches the question.

help.concept: Use the box-model concept named in the lesson rather than guessing from visual appearance alone.
help.hint_1: Compare what happens inside the border with what happens outside it.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that matches the exact CSS responsibility described.

display-and-overflow-multi-2.title: Recognize horizontal overflow behavior
display-and-overflow-multi-2.hint: Evaluate each statement independently against the lesson. More than one choice may be correct.

help.concept: A multi-select can have several correct statements.
help.hint_1: Check each statement independently against the prompt.
help.hint_2: Select every statement that is fully correct and leave the others unselected.

options.a: It can allow horizontal scrolling when content is too wide.
options.b: It controls overflow on the horizontal axis.
options.c: It automatically turns the element into a Grid container.

display-and-overflow-multi.title: Select every correct box-model idea
display-and-overflow-multi.prompt: What can inline-block provide to an inline-flow element?
display-and-overflow-multi.hint: Evaluate each option independently against the definition in the lesson. More than one choice may be correct.

help.concept: A multi-select question can have more than one correct choice.
help.hint_1: Check each choice independently instead of assuming only one is correct.
help.hint_2: Select only the choices that satisfy the definition stated in the prompt.

display-and-overflow-reorder.title: Put the box-model idea in order
display-and-overflow-reorder.prompt: Order a clean overflow troubleshooting process.
display-and-overflow-reorder.hint: Start with the first conceptual or physical step and move outward or forward.

help.concept: Ordering helps make the CSS relationship explicit instead of memorizing disconnected terms.
help.hint_1: Identify the item that must come first.
help.hint_2: Then place each remaining item in the sequence described by the lesson.

tokens.t1: identify the box that is too wide
tokens.t3: apply overflow to the responsible container

display-and-overflow-fill-1.prompt: Choose the term that makes the statement correct.
display-and-overflow-fill-1.hint: Match the missing term to the lesson's box-model definition.

help.concept: Match the missing term to the exact CSS concept described by the sentence.
help.hint_1: Read what part of the box or behavior the sentence is describing.
help.hint_2: Choose the property or value that performs that responsibility.

display-and-overflow-fill-1.template: To keep an element in inline flow while giving it box behavior, use [blank1].

display-and-overflow-fill-2.title: Complete the second CSS statement
display-and-overflow-fill-2.prompt: Choose the term that makes the statement correct.
display-and-overflow-fill-2.hint: Use the precise property or value described in the sentence.

help.concept: Match the missing term to the exact CSS concept described by the sentence.
help.hint_1: Read what part of the box or behavior the sentence is describing.
help.hint_2: Choose the property or value that performs that responsibility.

try-display-and-overflow-sketch0.title: Give navigation links box-like behavior
try-display-and-overflow-sketch0.prompt:
**Problem**

Navigation links behave like ordinary inline text, so their box behavior is limited even though later styling needs each link to accept box-model spacing and sizing.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `display: inline-block;` to a `nav a` rule.
try-display-and-overflow-sketch0.hint: Change only the display behavior of the existing navigation links.

help.concept: inline-block keeps an element in inline flow while allowing it to behave like a box for spacing and sizing.
help.hint_2: Only the `display` property needs to change in this step.

try-display-and-overflow-card-surfaces.title: Turn main content groups into card surfaces
try-display-and-overflow-card-surfaces.prompt:
**Problem**

The main sections and articles still blend into the page instead of reading as distinct content surfaces.

**Task**

Keep every previous rule. Style `main section, main article` with `border: 1px solid #cbd5e1;`, `padding: 1.25rem;`, and `margin-block: 1rem;`.
try-display-and-overflow-card-surfaces.hint: Use one shared selector for the existing main sections and articles, then give that surface an edge, inner space, and outside separation.

help.concept: A reusable content surface can combine one border, inner padding, and outside separation under a shared selector.
help.hint_1: Use the existing `main section, main article` selector pair.
help.hint_2: Keep the three declarations together because they describe one card-surface responsibility.

try-display-and-overflow-form-surface.title: Give the form a constrained surface
try-display-and-overflow-form-surface.prompt:
**Problem**

The form still stretches without a clear visual boundary, so it does not read as a focused input surface.

**Task**

Keep all previous CSS. Add a `form` rule with `max-width: 36rem;`, `padding: 1.5rem;`, and `border: 1px solid #cbd5e1;`.
try-display-and-overflow-form-surface.hint: Constrain the existing form and give its container inner space plus a visible edge.

help.concept: A constrained form surface uses a readable maximum width plus its own inner spacing and visible boundary.
help.hint_2: Keep max-width, padding, and border together on the form container.

try-display-and-overflow-table-width.title: Let the table use the available width
try-display-and-overflow-table-width.prompt:
**Problem**

The table can scroll when needed, but it does not yet use the full width available inside its container.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `width: 100%;` to a `table` rule.
try-display-and-overflow-table-width.hint: Keep the overflow behavior and make the existing table fill its available container width.

help.concept: A percentage width can let the existing table use the available width of its container.
help.hint_1: Target the table without removing its earlier overflow behavior.
help.hint_2: Add only the width responsibility in this step.

try-display-and-overflow-centered-image.title: Center the inherited image as a block
try-display-and-overflow-centered-image.prompt:
**Problem**

The inherited image still participates in inline flow, which makes simple horizontal centering unreliable.

**Task**

Keep every previous rule. Add an `img` rule with `display: block;` and `margin-inline: auto;`.
try-display-and-overflow-centered-image.hint: A block-level image can use automatic inline margins for horizontal centering.

help.concept: A block-level image can be centered horizontally with automatic inline margins.
help.hint_2: Use block display first, then automatic inline margins.
